QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_24

question.text: An investment adviser has a client, Mrs. Lakshmi, who is an ROR. She has the following incomes: (i) Salary from Indian employer: Rs.12,00,000, (ii) Interest on NRE fixed deposit: Rs.80,000, (iii) Dividend from UK company received in UK: Rs.1,50,000, (iv) Rental income from property in Singapore: Rs.2,40,000. Based on the workbook text, which incomes are taxable in India?

answer.text: Only (i) and (ii) — salary and NRE interest
Only (i), (iii) and (iv) — salary, UK dividend, and Singapore rental income
All four incomes (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are taxable
Only (i) — salary; the rest are foreign or exempt incomes

explanation.text: The Logic: An ROR (Resident and Ordinarily Resident) is taxable on worldwide income. (i) Indian salary — taxable. (iii) UK dividend received in UK — worldwide income, taxable for ROR. (iv) Singapore rental income — worldwide income, taxable for ROR. (ii) Interest on NRE fixed deposit is listed by the workbook as exempt under section 10(4)(ii); the checked workbook text treats this exemption without an explicit ROR/FEMA carve-out, so on the workbook text alone the NRE interest is not taxable in this question. The Trap: Candidates often assume all four are taxable solely because the client is ROR, ignoring the specific exemption the workbook lists for NRE account interest. Equally, candidates may exempt all foreign income and overlook that ROR are taxed on worldwide income. Note: The NRE interest treatment in this item follows the workbook's section 10(4)(ii) text. Status changes from NR to resident under FEMA can affect eligibility to hold an NRE account; consult the latest FEMA rules and bank documentation before relying on the exemption in practice.
